summary: Tenant pin oscillation after quota-driven preemptive autoscale causes mixed-model routing
description:
Issue summary:

During a customer-triggered traffic surge last night, tenant sessions for NimbusHealth experienced repeated model-version pin oscillations after the autoscaler performed quota-driven preemptive GPU rebalancing. Traffic for affected sessions alternated between the pinned variant (gptx-7b-v1) and a degraded fallback (gptx-7b-v1-quant) causing mixed outputs and a visible quality regression for the customer.

Impact:
- ~18% of requests from the tenant in us-east-1 returned responses from the quantized fallback variant during a 22-minute window.
- Several long-lived streaming sessions were truncated (stream closed mid-response) and retried, leading to increased token counts and billing anomalies.
- Customer-facing SLA alerts for latency and output quality were triggered.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant pin should hold for the session cohort during autoscaler preemptive operations unless an explicit orchestrator demotion occurs.
- Fallback routing should only be taken during node failure or explicit health probe evictions, not as a side-effect of quota preemption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated pool with quota policy set to aggressive_preempt (customer-simulated).
2) Start 30 long-lived streaming sessions pinned to gptx-7b-v1 for a single tenant in us-east-1.
3) Trigger a quota-driven autoscale event by increasing unrelated tenant traffic to exhaust GPU headroom, causing preemptive rebalancing.
4) Observe routing decisions in request traces and model variant field in responses over the next 30 minutes.

comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer reported quality regressions and elevated token usage during their nightly load test. Attached traces show version field flipping between variants within session lifetimes. Escalating to SRE and Serving team.

SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-10: Reproduced on a staging replica of the customer's pool using aggressive_preempt. Observed orchestrator epoch jump correlated with autoscaler preemptive job. Hypothesis: preempt triggers a fast rebind path that does not wait for pin consensus, allowing the edge to reassign to standby variant under certain timing windows.

Serving (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Found evidence of kv-cache TTL mismatches across serving instances. When preempt rebinds sessions to a new host, the new host's cache lacks the pinned metadata and request routing falls back to compatibility variant. Opening a PR to add pin->cache warmup handshake and stronger pin persistence during preempt operations. Related PR: GH-Redwood/serving#2679.

Customer (NimbusHealth - Alex Reed) 2026-03-11: Impact verified on our side — model outputs changed mid-session on critical test flows. We saw increased token counts when retries happened. Appreciate ETA and temporary mitigations.

SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-12: Implemented temporary mitigation: inhibit preemptive rebind for cohorts with active streaming sessions older than 60s while we validate the pin-warmup fix. This reduced oscillation in canary runs. Working with Serving team for permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator performs epoch advancement and issues rebinds before edge/serving cache synchronization completes. Leads to missing pin metadata on new serving hosts.

Hypothesis 2: Aggressive preempt policy bypasses normal graceful drain path and invokes a fast-path that does not honor pin handshake. Evidence: logs show preemptive_rebalance vs graceful_drain timestamps overlapping with session activity.
Telemetry: Trace sampling shows 27% of route decisions during the window were handled by nodes with last_cache_sync > 30s, correlates with fallback events.
Reproducible: Yes, staging repro by running aggressive_preempt with long-lived streams. Failure mode appears timing-sensitive — adding artificial 50ms delay to rebind reduced incidence in tests.

Related artifacts: Dashboards: /dashboards/tenant-routing/us-east-1, Traces: /traces/tenant/nimbus-42/2026-03-10, PR: GH-Redwood/serving#2679 (pin-warmup), Runbook snippet: CONFLUENCE-RT/pin-fallback-handling.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: preempt inhibit for active streaming cohorts >60s and added extra cache-sync confirmation in the preempt workflow. Serving team merged pin-warmup handshake (GH-Redwood/serving#2679) to staging; rolling canary to production scheduled 2026-03-13 with a monitored gradual ramp. Post-deploy monitoring thresholds: <=1% fallback rate for pinned cohorts and no stream truncations. Follow-ups: add telemetry metric for pin_consensus_latency and update orchestration runbook with explicit preempt safety gates.
next_steps: 1) Roll out GH-Redwood/serving#2679 to canary pools on 2026-03-13 and monitor fallback_rate and stream_close_rate closely.
2) Instrument pin_consensus_latency metric and add alert when >200ms for any cohort in prod.
3) Update orchestration runbook to disallow preemptive rebinds for cohorts with active streaming sessions unless emergency flag set.
4) Postmortem doc planned and will be linked here after completion.
